branch.hint: Switch mode picks one of N branches; if-else mode runs `then` when the evaluator is truthy and `else` otherwise. Deterministic — no LLM call.

modeHint.switch: Pick the best branch from the upstream step's input via a selector (function / CEL / HITL).
modeHint.if-else: Run the connected `then` target only when the evaluator returns truthy against the upstream step's input.

selectorModeHint.function: Run a Python expression against the upstream step. Return the chosen branch step object (e.g. `na_faq_step`). No LLM call.
selectorModeHint.cel: Pass a CEL expression string to agno. Must return a branch label (e.g. `"na_faq_step"`). Requires `cel-python` at runtime.
selectorModeHint.hitl: Pause execution and ask the user to pick the branch. No LLM call — agno presents the choices to the user.

evaluatorModeHint.function: Write a Python expression evaluated against step_input. 5 locals are in scope: previous_step_content, previous_step_outputs, input, additional_data, session_state.
evaluatorModeHint.cel: Write a CEL (Common Expression Language) string passed verbatim to agno. Returns a boolean. Requires cel-python.
evaluatorModeHint.literal: Pick a constant True or False value.

branch.expressionPlaceholder: na_faq_step if 'billing' in previous_step_content else na_support_step
branch.expressionHint: 5 locals in scope: previous_step_content, previous_step_outputs, input, additional_data, session_state.
branch.celHint: Returns a branch label (switch) or boolean (if-else). CEL docs: https://github.com/google/cel-spec
branch.hitlPromptHint: Shown to the user when agno pauses for branch selection. Empty = agno's default prompt listing the choices.
branch.thenHint: The first outgoing edge from this node.
branch.elseHint: Optional. Runs when the condition is false.
branch.requiresConfirmationLabel: Ask user to confirm the then-branch before evaluating

parallel.hint: Branches are wired by connecting edges from this node to the targets.

flow.hint: Branches are wired by connecting edges from this node to the targets.
flow.hitlHint: Pause the whole block and ask for confirmation BEFORE the first step runs. One prompt — not per-step.
flow.hitlHintParallel: Ignored in `parallel` mode — switch to `sequential` to enable the block-level confirmation gate.

steps.hint: Run branches in sequence — edge order is the execution order. Connect edges from this node to the steps you want to chain.
steps.hitlHint: Pause the whole block and ask for confirmation BEFORE the first step runs. One prompt — not per-step.

loop.hint: Repeat the chosen step up to N times. Stops early when the iteration output contains the end-condition substring.
loop.endConditionHint: Substring matched against the iteration's output. Leave empty to always run max iterations.
loop.forwardLabel: Feed each iteration's output into the next iteration's input
loop.bodyHint: The step that runs each iteration. Edges from the loop node are what runs AFTER the loop.
loop.hitlHint: Pause the loop and ask for confirmation before running. Two independent checkpoints: once at the start, and once per iteration.

tpl-hello-world.name: Hello World
tpl-hello-world.description: The simplest possible workflow — input feeds an agent, whose reply flows to the output.

tpl-ask-the-user.name: Ask the User
tpl-ask-the-user.description: An ask gate pauses the workflow to collect user input, then a final agent answers based on the user's response.

tpl-conditional-greeting.name: Conditional Greeting
tpl-conditional-greeting.description: If-else branch reads the workflow input directly — if the input contains 'urgent' the urgent responder replies, otherwise the casual one.

tpl-iterative-story.name: Iterative Story Generator
tpl-iterative-story.description: A writer agent self-iterates up to 3 times — drafts the opening scene on the first run, then self-critiques and revises on each subsequent iteration (stops when the writer outputs 'DONE').

tpl-parallel-summary.name: Parallel Research with Synthesis
tpl-parallel-summary.description: Two agents analyze the input from opposing angles in parallel; a sibling synthesizer combines their findings into one balanced answer.
